blocks.text: Intermolecular forces are also considered binding forces, like chemical bonds, but the attraction between molecules is much weaker than a chemical bond. These forces are believed to exist between all kinds of atoms and molecules when they are sufficiently close to each other, and are called van der Waals forces. They bring the molecules close together and give particular physical properties to substances in the gaseous, liquid and solid states. Three types are mentioned here; the detailed discussion comes in the chapter on states and phases of matter.

items: Instantaneous dipole-induced dipole forces, or London dispersion forces.

blocks.prompt: Which of the three intermolecular forces would you expect between HCl molecules, and which between the molecules of a noble gas such as argon?
blocks.explanation: HCl molecules are permanent dipoles, so permanent dipole-permanent dipole forces act between them (with London forces as well). Argon atoms have no permanent dipole, so only instantaneous dipole-induced dipole forces, the London dispersion forces, hold them together.

items: Van der Waals (intermolecular) forces are weak binding forces between molecules that set the physical properties of gases, liquids and solids: London dispersion, permanent dipole-dipole and hydrogen bonding.
